Executive Order

MOobDIFYING THE CopDE OF Farr COMPETITION FOR THE BAKING INDUSTRY
AND THE ORDER OF APPROVAL THEREOF

ORDER NO. 445-2

WHEREAS, certain facts have heen submitted by members of the Baking
Industry indicating the necessity of certain modifications in the Code of Fair Competi-
tion for said Industry, as approved by me on May 28, 1934; and

WHEREAS, it appears necessary in the public interest to make such modifica-
tions in order to effectuate the purposes of the Act;

NOW, THEREFORE, I, Franklin D. Roosevelt, President of the United States,
pursuant to the authority vested in me by Title I of the National Industrial Recovery
Act, upon due consideration of the facts and upon the recommendation of the Adminis-
trator for Industrial Recovery, hereby order:

1. That the effective date of the Code of Fair Competition for the Baking Indus-
try be and the same hereby is stayed until July 9, 1934;

2. That the second condition of the Order of May 28, 1934, approving the said
code, staying the provisions of Article VII, Section 6, until my further order, is hereby
eliminated and the provisions of said section shall be in full force and effect on the
effective date of said code.

3. That the period within which the Code Authority is to report its investiga-
tion of the operation and the effect of the provisions of Articles III, IV, and V to me
is hereby extended from the date designated in said order of approval to November

15, 1934.
FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

Approval recommended:
Hvuas S JoHnson
Administrator

Tue Waits House
June 16, 1984.

[No. 6743]

versions.research_rationale:
EO 6743 (dated June 16, 1934 in the held text, Franklin D. Roosevelt) modifies the Code of Fair Competition for the Baking Industry and the order of May 28, 1934 approving it, under title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act. Read in full in the held American Presidency Project transcription (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-6743-modifying-the-code-fair-competition-for-the-baking-industry-and-the.txt, 1,461 characters, grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; the transcription contains optical-character errors such as 'hi' for 'in' and 'tlie' for 'the'). APP page check (AGENT_PROTOCOL.md, working-text paragraph): the jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl row with sha256 60264df5166bf6bd33c72dbf237c46a37988747d9bfc2f264574fc066810fa80 is headed 'Executive Order 6743—Modifying the Code of Fair Competition for the Baking Industry and the Order of Approval Thereof', dated June 16, 1934, node app:node/362518, Common Crawl capture 2025-06-16T14:01:16Z; its text_sha256 bde24fb91473b071f55815d78cfc6157911799116059171c33875ce13083da17 equals the sha256 I computed for the held file, and the page heading, the date and the subject agree with the text. Cotton holds the exact page bytes (jobs/cotton-capture-custody/output/captures). Identity also agrees with the census register row and the WPA 1944 list (page 581: 'Code of Fair Competition for the Baking Industry modified. XII NRA Codes 247.'). The WPA list dates the order June 15, 1934; the page heading, the census register and the held text all say June 16, 1934. The one-day difference does not change identity (number, subject and the NRA Codes citation agree) and enters no end date below, because every end is keyed to the order's own stated July 9, 1934 or to the June 14, 1935 repeal. The order has three numbered operative clauses, which I have read separately: (1) 'the effective date of the Code of Fair Competition for the Baking Industry be and the same hereby is stayed until July 9, 1934'; (2) the second condition of the approving order, which stayed a provision of article VII 'until my further order', 'is hereby eliminated and the provisions of said section shall be ... in full force and effect on the effective date of said code' (the held text reads 'Section G'; the approving order of May 28, 1934, held as a separate APP text, states the stayed provision as 'Section 6', so 'G' is evidently a transcription error for '6'; the lifecycle does not depend on which section); (3) the period in which the Code Authority is to report on the operation and effect of articles III, IV and V 'is hereby extended from the date designated in said order of approval to November 15, 1934'. The machine inventory (three clauses, characters 654 to 789, 791 to 1074 and 1076 to 1426) is complete and correct; the lead-in recital, the 'ORDER NO. 445-2' heading and the signature block command nothing, so no replacement inventory is needed. The dossier's own-terms leads are right for clause 1 (a stated date, July 9, 1934) and clause 3 (a report deadline), and wording matches only for clause 2 ('until my further order' describes the stay that clause 2 removes; clause 2 itself states no period).

The machine searches of the U.S. Code and eCFR (complete, 0 hits) exclude a current-law reference; the OFR catalog search starts in 1937 and is not relied on alone. The only held orders naming the baking code are the approving order of May 28, 1934 (EO 6725-A, whose government printed copy is not held; the number 6725 in the government printed volume belongs to an unrelated Science Advisory Board order) and this order. No held record shows this code cancelled, modified under section 10(b), superseded, suspended or stayed before June 14, 1935. Later orders that act on Title I generally, of June 15, 1935 (the reorganization of the NRA and the order extending Title I activities to April 1, 1936 'so far as consistent' with Title I as amended, whose proviso disclaims any authority to approve or prescribe codes or to provide for their enforcement), post-date the repeal and do not continue a code approval. Amendments are later events, not ends; June 16, 1935 is not an end, because section 1 of the resolution replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936. Clause 1 has an own-terms end before June 14, 1935 (July 9, 1934), which is its first end. For clauses 2 and 3 no earlier end is held; in particular nothing held modifies, stays or cancels the modification after June 16, 1934.","independent_command_check":"None of the three clauses is independent of the code. Clause 1 stays the code's own effective date; clause 2 lifts a condition of the approval of the code; clause 3 adjusts the reporting duty of the Code Authority, a body that exists only under the approved code (the approving order imposes the report). The order makes no appointment, creates no committee or board, delegates nothing under another statute and directs no agency, and no clause here is a stay 'pending further order' (clause 2 removes one), so no independent command is retained and the order is not a mixed order.","savings_check":"Clause 1: once the stay ran through July 9, 1934 the code's effective date arrived and the code took effect; that is a completed effect of the stay and keeps nothing of the stay operative. Clauses 2 and 3: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the code before June 14, 1935 are completed (accrued) effects of the approval; the general savings statute of the time, which ordinarily preserves liabilities incurred under a repealed statute, is not a held source, and the repeal text contains no savings clause. Section 5 of title I exempted from the antitrust laws any code approved and in effect under the title and any action complying with it taken during the period; the resolution's proviso limits that exemption to agreements and action thereunder of two stated kinds and states no time limit, so the held text does not settle whether it narrowed the exemption for action taken under codes before June 14, 1935. Whatever exemption or liability survives for past action is an accrued effect of completed acts, not continued operation of this approval. No held source shows a prosecution, injunction or other proceeding under this code continuing after June 14, 1935, and nothing continues the approval itself.","scope_check":"Three separate commands, each given its own end: a stay of the code's effective date to a fixed date (clause 1), the removal of a condition that stayed one provision of the approval (clause 2), and the extension of a reporting date for the Code Authority (clause 3). Clause 1 is a stay to a fixed date before June 14, 1935, so its own-terms end controls. The extension in clause 3 moves a deadline: a report deadline is not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21, report deadlines), so the November 15, 1934 date is recorded as a spent fact, 'functionally spent on November 15, 1934', and the clause's end is the repeal that removed the approval the Code Authority's duty rested on; no held record shows whether the Code Authority reported by that date. No partial event inside any clause is held or found."}

Clauses 2 and 3: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the code before June 14, 1935 are completed (accrued) effects of the approval; the general savings statute of the time, which ordinarily preserves liabilities incurred under a repealed statute, is not a held source, and the repeal text contains no savings clause. Section 5 of title I exempted from the antitrust laws any code approved and in effect under the title and any action complying with it taken during the period; the resolution's proviso limits that exemption to agreements and action thereunder of two stated kinds and states no time limit, so the held text does not settle whether it narrowed the exemption for action taken under codes before June 14, 1935. Whatever exemption or liability survives for past action is an accrued effect of completed acts, not continued operation of this approval. No held source shows a prosecution, injunction or other proceeding under this code continuing after June 14, 1935, and nothing continues the approval itself.
